h1: Life in the UK practice test
intro: Take a free Life in the UK practice test with 24 questions, a 45-minute timer and instant marking, just like the real thing. Every Life in the UK practice test picks new questions at random, so you can keep practising until you’re ready.
cardText: Free 24-question practice tests with instant marking.

sections.heading: How the Life in the UK practice test works
sections.text:
Each test has 24 multiple-choice questions and a 45-minute countdown, the same as the real test. You need 18 correct answers, which is 75%, to pass.

At the end you see your score and every question you got wrong, with the right answer and a short explanation. Switch on learning mode to see the answer after each question instead.

sections.heading: What the questions cover
sections.text:
Our questions cover the same topics as the official handbook, Life in the United Kingdom: A Guide for New Residents:
- The values and principles of the UK
- What the UK is, its countries and its symbols
- British history, from the Stone Age to the present day
- Modern society, including festivals, sport, arts and famous people
- The UK government, the law and your role

We write our own practice questions. The real test questions aren’t published, so no practice test can guarantee you’ll see the same ones.

sections.heading: Sample questions
sections.text:
Here are three questions like the ones in our Life in the UK practice test:
- In which year was the National Health Service set up? Answer: 1948.
- Who is the patron saint of Wales? Answer: St David, celebrated on 1 March.
- How often must a general election be held? Answer: at least every five years.

The full practice test above has dozens more, picked at random each time.

sections.heading: Tips for passing first time
sections.text:
- Read the official handbook from start to finish at least once. Every real question comes from it.
- Take a Life in the UK practice test every day for a week or two before your test.
- Learn dates for the big events in British history, as they come up often.
- Read every option carefully. Some questions ask which statement is true, and some ask you to pick two answers.
- Book your test early, so you have your pass before you apply.

sections.heading: Booking the real test
sections.text: You book the Life in the UK test online through GOV.UK, at least 3 days before you want to take it. It costs £50, and you take it at an approved test centre with the same ID you booked with. Read our guide to the [Life in the UK test](/life-in-the-uk-test/) for more on booking and the day itself.

sections.heading: After you pass
sections.text: You get a unique reference number, which you need for your [Indefinite Leave to Remain](/indefinite-leave-to-remain/) or [British citizenship](/british-citizenship/) application. You only need to pass once, and your pass doesn’t expire. If you’re planning to apply soon, our advisers can check you meet every requirement first.

faqs.q: Is the Life in the UK practice test free?
faqs.a: Yes. Take as many practice tests as you like, with no sign-up.

faqs.q: How many questions are in the real Life in the UK test?
faqs.a: 24 questions in 45 minutes. You need 18 correct answers to pass.

faqs.q: Are these the real test questions?
faqs.a: No. The real questions aren’t published. Ours are written to cover the same topics as the official handbook.

faqs.q: How many times can I take the real test?
faqs.a: As many times as you need, but you pay £50 each time and must wait at least 7 days between attempts.

faqs.q: Who needs to pass the Life in the UK test?
faqs.a: Most people aged 18 to 64 applying for Indefinite Leave to Remain or British citizenship.
